trust_decision.summary: The length returned by jsvGetString() is trusted as an in-bounds index into the caller's fixed buffer. When the string is cropped, the iterator branch returns len instead of len-1, and jslGetTokenValueAsString() then writes the terminating 0 at token[64], one byte past the end.

landing_point.why: The advisory names jslGetTokenValueAsString(), and the out-of-bounds null write is on this line.

fix_sites.entry_point: jsvGetString(), the core public C API used by about 97 call sites; reached from JS via any string-to-buffer conversion of a non-flat string longer than the buffer
fix_sites.module_kind: lower-level core variable API (another file from the landing point)

fix_sites.entry_point: jslGetTokenValueAsString(), reached by the JS parser (eval/REPL/uploaded code), Date.parse (src/jswrap_date.c:1014-1019) and JSON number parsing (src/jswrap_json.c:104)
fix_sites.module_kind: lexer (the fix only removed the redundant null write)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/jsvar.c:1540-1544 (jsvGetString iterator branch returns len on crop)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: jsvGetString is documented as cropping and null-terminating safely (src/jsvar.h:498), so a solver clamps tokenl in the lexer and treats the off-by-one return value as a documented quirk of a core API.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Pretokenised reserved words take tokenl==0 and rebuild the name from the reserved-word table; an over-broad change to the tokenl==0 handling, or to jsvGetString's crop semantics, breaks keyword names and the cropping that callers rely on (for example ssid_len).

O6_input_shapes: non-flat / multi-block string token (iterator branch of jsvGetString) longer than 63 chars
raw (pretokenised) string token whose tokenl is 0 and tokenValue is set (src/jslex.c:603-617)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A core (Linux-buildable) caller that indexes its buffer with jsvGetString's return value, like targets/esp32/jswrap_rtos.c:40, so a lexer-only fix leaves an observable OOB.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The pattern name[jsvGetString(...)] = 0 already exists three times in targets/esp32/jswrap_rtos.c:40,106,197.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A wrapper over jsvGetStringChars that null-terminates at the returned length without the clamp done at src/jsvar.c:1557.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: jsvGetStringChars returns len on truncation by design, and only one caller clamps it today.

O9_family: memory-safety: off-by-one out-of-bounds write (CWE-787, CWE-193) from length-return arithmetic

O10_build.toolchain: make/gcc (Linux host build of the interpreter), Python for wrapper generation
O10_build.project_tests: tests/*.js run by the Linux build (e.g. tests/test_pretokenise.js, tests/test_pretokenise2.js, tests/test_pretokenise3.js); no test added by the fix

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Clamp lex->tokenl to JSLEX_MAX_TOKEN_LENGTH-1 in jslGetTokenValueAsString and leave jsvGetString's return value wrong.

out_of_scope_notes: jsvGetString's int branch calls itostr without a len bound (src/jsvar.c:1528-1530); not checked whether any caller passes a buffer under about 12 bytes.
unverified: Every caller that indexes with, or uses, jsvGetString's return value is outside the Linux build (targets/esp32/jswrap_rtos.c:40,106,197; libs/network/esp32/jswrap_esp32_network.c:1387; libs/network/esp8266/jswrap_esp8266_network.c:547; libs/bluetooth/jswrap_bluetooth.c:1092,1606; targets/nrf5x/bluetooth.c:3164). On Linux the only observable OOB seems to be src/jslex.c:1141, so hidden tests probably cannot tell a lexer-only fix from the root-cause fix. This was not fully verified across all 97 call sites.

Exactly which lexer paths leave tokenl==0 with a non-flat tokenValue longer than 63 chars (raw/pretokenised strings at src/jslex.c:603-617, template literals at src/jslex.c:518) was not traced end to end.
